decisions.decision: Implemented the classic 'slow' Stochastic Oscillator construction: fast %K = 100*(close-LL)/(HH-LL) over a rolling k_period window, %K = simple moving average (rolling().mean(), not ewm) of fast %K over `smooth` bars, %D = simple moving average of %K over `d_period` bars. All three windows use pandas rolling/SMA, not the EMA-based smoothing used by ema.py/macd.py/force_index.py elsewhere in this app.
decisions.rationale: docs/Analyse.md §4 lists Stochastic's parameters as '%K 5, %D 3, smooth 3' -- three distinct values, which only makes sense under the classic fast-%K -> smoothed-%K -> %D construction (an EMA-only reading would have no third parameter to hang 'smooth' off of). This is also the standard textbook/Elder definition of the Stochastic Oscillator, which historically uses SMA smoothing, unlike Force Index/MACD/EMA which are explicitly EMA-based in Analyse.md's own prose. Rejected treating 'smooth' as an alternate/EMA period for %K (would collapse to a 2-parameter indicator and ignores the doc's explicit 3-parameter listing).
decisions.rejected: Considered reusing app/indicators/ema.py's ewm-based smoothing for %K/%D (for consistency with the rest of the codebase's EMA-heavy style), but rejected it because it would silently diverge from both Analyse.md's parameter list and the textbook Stochastic definition, which is exactly the kind of library-formula-vs-book-definition mismatch docs/architecture/Backend.md §1/§4 calls out as the reason indicators are hand-written per their Analyse.md definition rather than assumed from a generic pattern.

decisions.decision: A flat trailing range (HH == LL over the k_period window, so fast %K is a 0/0 division) is left as NaN rather than special-cased to 0 or 50.
decisions.rationale: pandas/numpy already produces NaN for a 0.0/0.0 division on float Series with no extra code, and NaN is the same 'undefined, not yet actionable' signal this app already uses for EMA/Force Index warm-up periods -- consistent with how downstream Screen 2 wave logic (not yet implemented) should already be handling NaN oscillator values before a series is fully warmed up.
decisions.rejected: Considered clamping to 50 (a common 'neutral' convention in some TA libraries) but rejected it as inventing a value Analyse.md doesn't specify, for an edge case (a perfectly flat multi-bar range) unlikely to occur in real daily OHLCV data anyway.

comments.summary: Non-blocking (reuse/simplification, from code-review skill): _validate_period's int/bool/range guard in stochastic.py duplicates the identical inline check in app/indicators/ema.py::ema(). force_index.py avoided this by delegating to ema() directly, but stochastic.py can't (it's SMA-, not EMA-, based), so this needs its own follow-up -- e.g. a shared _validate_period-style helper -- once a third indicator (elder_ray, autoenvelope) needs the same guard. Not blocking.
